articles.headline: OFAC Announces Settlement with Pegasus Worldwide Logistics, Designates International Criminal Court Officials, and Removes Burma-Related Designations
body: The U.S. Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced a settlement agreement with Pegasus Worldwide Logistics. Concurrently, OFAC designated individuals associated with the International Criminal Court (ICC) and issued related General Licenses.

In a separate action, OFAC also removed certain designations related to Burma, indicating a shift in specific sanctions targets within that program. These actions reflect OFAC's ongoing efforts to enforce sanctions while also adapting to evolving geopolitical circumstances and engaging in targeted removals where appropriate.

articles.headline: OFAC Issues New Russia-Related General License
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) has issued a new General License pertaining to Russia-related activities. This new license aims to provide specific authorizations for certain transactions that would otherwise be prohibited under existing Russia sanctions programs.

The issuance of General Licenses often indicates an effort by OFAC to clarify the scope of sanctions or to permit certain humanitarian, administrative, or other specific activities that are deemed not to undermine the overall policy objectives of the sanctions regime.

articles.headline: OFAC Imposes New Iran-Related Designations, Issues General License, and Amends Russia-Related General License
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced new designations targeting entities and individuals connected to Iran. These actions are part of ongoing efforts to counter Iran's destabilizing activities and its nuclear program.

In conjunction with these new designations, OFAC also issued a new Iran-related General License, which may permit certain transactions that would otherwise be prohibited. Additionally, an existing Russia-related General License was amended, indicating adjustments to the scope of authorized activities under the Russia sanctions program.

articles.headline: OFAC Announces Designations Removals and Updates, Publishes Iran-Related Alert and Amended FAQ
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) has announced several designations removals and updates to its sanctions lists. These changes reflect ongoing evaluations of individuals and entities previously sanctioned.

Furthermore, OFAC published an Iran-related Alert and an Amended Iran-related Frequently Asked Question (FAQ). These publications aim to provide updated guidance and information to the public regarding the Iran sanctions program, helping to ensure compliance and clarify policy.

articles.headline: OFAC Imposes New Counter Terrorism Designations
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced new designations under its counter-terrorism sanctions program. These actions target individuals and entities identified as supporting terrorist organizations or engaging in terrorism-related activities.

These designations aim to disrupt the financial networks of terrorist groups and prevent them from accessing the international financial system. OFAC continues to prioritize counter-terrorism efforts as a key component of its national security mission.

articles.headline: OFAC Designates Iran-Related Entities and Transnational Criminal Organizations, Issues Determination and Amended FAQ
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced new designations targeting entities and individuals linked to Iran, as well as those involved in transnational criminal organizations. These actions underscore the U.S. government's commitment to combating illicit financial activities and state-sponsored illicit networks.

In conjunction with these designations, OFAC published an Iran-related Determination and an Amended Iran-related Frequently Asked Question (FAQ). These documents provide further clarity and legal basis for the new measures, as well as updated guidance for compliance with Iran sanctions.

articles.headline: OFAC Designates Counter Terrorism and Transnational Criminal Organizations, Removes Belarus, Counter Narcotics, and Libya Designations
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced new designations targeting individuals and entities involved in counter-terrorism and transnational criminal organizations. These actions aim to disrupt illicit financial networks globally.

In a separate but related move, OFAC also removed several designations related to Belarus, counter narcotics efforts, and Libya. These removals indicate a reassessment of specific targets within these sanctions programs, potentially reflecting changes in behavior or policy.

articles.headline: OFAC Imposes New Counter Narcotics, Counter Terrorism, Iran-Related, and Non-Proliferation Designations
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced a series of new designations across multiple sanctions programs, targeting individuals and entities involved in counter narcotics, counter terrorism, Iran-related activities, and non-proliferation efforts.

These comprehensive actions demonstrate OFAC's broad approach to combating various threats to U.S. national security and foreign policy. The designations aim to disrupt illicit networks and prevent the flow of funds and resources to these illicit activities.

articles.headline: OFAC Publishes Regulatory Amendments, New Cuba Sanctions Regulations, Amended FAQs, and Cuba-Related Alert
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) has published significant regulatory amendments, including new Cuba Sanctions Regulations. These updates reflect a comprehensive review and adjustment of U.S. policy towards Cuba.

In addition to the new regulations, OFAC issued new and amended Cuba-related Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs) and a Cuba-related OFAC Alert. These resources are intended to provide clarity and guidance to the public regarding the updated sanctions framework and compliance expectations for transactions involving Cuba.

articles.headline: OFAC Issues Amended Venezuela General Licenses
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) has issued amended Venezuela General Licenses. These amendments modify existing authorizations for certain transactions and activities related to Venezuela.

The issuance of amended General Licenses often signals adjustments in U.S. policy, aiming to either tighten or ease specific restrictions while maintaining the overall sanctions framework. Entities engaging in Venezuela-related activities should review these amendments carefully for compliance.

articles.headline: UK Imposes New Sanctions on Russia Targeting Oil, Financial Services, and Military Supply Chains
body: Britain's Foreign Office announced a new round of sanctions against Russia, targeting 38 individuals and entities involved in the production or transport of Russian oil, facilitating military manufacturing, and circumventing financial services sanctions.

The package includes sanctions on 12 oil tankers operating as part of Russia's 'shadow fleet,' three crypto exchanges, two payment platforms suspected of being used to bypass financial sanctions, and 17 entities and individuals supplying goods critical to Russia's war effort. These measures aim to further restrict Russia's ability to fund and equip its military operations in Ukraine.
Russia's embassy in London criticized the new sanctions, stating that they are ineffective and futile, according to a report by RIA Novosti.

articles.headline: Global Bond Markets Under Pressure Amid Rising Yields and Energy Prices
body: Global bond markets are experiencing significant pressure, with borrowing costs for governments, businesses, and households increasing across major economies. In the U.S. and Japan, 10-year yields have reached multi-year highs, while Europe and the UK have also seen a substantial rise in borrowing costs.

Factors contributing to these rising yields include higher energy prices, persistent inflation concerns, and increasing government debt. The World Economic Forum's Centre for Financial and Monetary Systems highlights that higher yields can lead to more expensive mortgages and strain government funding for public services.
Despite these challenges, global fintech funding is surging, projected to reach a four-year high in 2026, with most of the investment flowing into larger fintech companies.

articles.headline: OCC Assesses $350 Million Penalty Against American Express National Bank for BSA/AML Failures
body: The Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (OCC) announced a cease-and-desist order and a $350 million civil money penalty against American Express National Bank for significant deficiencies in its Bank Secrecy Act (BSA) and anti-money laundering (AML) compliance program.

The OCC identified inadequate resources, insufficient staff expertise, systemic internal control gaps, weak independent testing, and a failure to tailor its BSA/AML risk assessment to its business activities, particularly its dominant credit and charge card products. These failures led to the bank not timely identifying, evaluating, and reporting approximately $13 billion of suspected trade-based money laundering activity over the past decade.

Comptroller of the Currency Jonathan Gould emphasized that banks of American Express's size and complexity are expected to dedicate sufficient resources to combat money laundering, which is crucial for economic and national security. The OCC's action is coordinated with a concurrent cease-and-desist order from the Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System against American Express Company and American Express Travel Related Services Company, Inc.
articles.source: Office of the Comptroller of the Currency

articles.headline: BIS Adds 29 Entities to Entity List, Including 19 from China, for National Security Concerns
body: The Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) has amended the Export Administration Regulations (EAR) by adding 29 entries to the Entity List. These additions include 19 entities from the People's Republic of China, 9 from Turkey, and 1 from the United Arab Emirates.

These entities have been determined by the U.S. Government to be acting contrary to the national security or foreign policy interests of the United States. The additions impose additional license requirements and limit the availability of most license exceptions for exports, reexports, and transfers (in-country) when a listed entity is a party to the transaction.

One notable addition is TGB Aviation, under the destination of Turkey, which is associated with the transshipment of U.S.-origin aircraft components into Iran, connected to the OFAC-designated Iran Aircraft Manufacturing Industries (HESA).

articles.headline: Streamlining Export Controls for Drone Exports
body: The Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) is easing export controls on certain Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs or drones) and related parts, components, accessories, attachments, technology, and software under the Export Administration Regulations (EAR). Specifically, this rule: eliminates wind gust tolerance as a parameter for determining UAV controls under the EAR; increases the threshold for national security controls on certain UAVs from an endurance of 30 minutes to an endurance of 3 hours; makes conforming changes to remove national security controls on software and technology associated with UAVs with an endurance less than 3 hours; maintains military end-use and end-user controls on those lower endurance drones and associated software and technology; clarifies Commerce Control List (CCL) controls for certain UAVs specially designed for military use; and removes national security controls on certain specially designed parts, components, accessories, and attachments for such UAVs as they do not provide any significant military or intelligence capabilities.

articles.headline: Implementation of EAR Export Controls on Silencers, Mufflers, and Sound Suppressors; and Other Firearms Related Changes
body: The Department of Commerce (Commerce), Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) is revising the Export Administration Regulations (EAR) and the Commerce Control List (CCL) to appropriately control certain silencers, mufflers, and sound suppressors (sound suppressors) that will no longer be described on the International Traffic in Arms Regulations U.S. Munitions List (USML). This interim final rule (IFR) complements a Department of State interim final rule published elsewhere in this issue of the Federal Register (International Traffic in Arms Regulations: USML Category I Firearm Suppressors (1400-AG11) (State IFR)). This transfer of jurisdiction will reduce the regulatory burden on exports of sound suppressors. This IFR also revises the EAR to allow firearms and related items to be temporarily exported and reexported under a license exception as tools of trade, thereby relieving exporters of the regulatory burden of applying for authorization. Finally, this IFR clarifies which items fall within the scope of the EAR's entry clearance requirements for a temporary import.

articles.headline: Enhanced Favorable Treatment for the United Arab Emirates Under the Export Administration Regulations
body: In this final rule, the Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) amends the Export Administration Regulations (EAR) to provide enhanced favorable treatment for the United Arab Emirates (UAE). Specifically, BIS is removing the UAE from Country Groups D:3 and D:4 and adding the UAE to Country Group A:5. More license exceptions will now be available, including Strategic Trade Authorization (STA) for the UAE Government and approved commercial entities in the UAE. STA will authorize the export, reexport, or transfer (in-country) of military items; certain commercial satellites and spacecraft; and dual-use items useful in, inter alia, oil and gas production, desalination, and civil nuclear power generation. The UAE Government and approved commercial entities will also have license-free access to advanced computing items, consistent with the May 2025 U.S.-UAE Artificial Intelligence Cooperation framework, without compromising U.S. digital infrastructure buildout.
